Abstract. The transport of phosphate is essential for the survival and growth of microorganisms.
PhoP is a key regulator of the phosphate-dependent transcriptional regulation in S. coelicolor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phosphate-dependent regulation of the two low-affinity and one high-affinity P(i)-transport systems is sequential, and the regulation of the two PitH transport systems is different.
PhoP is a global regulator of phosphate-dependent gene expression in Streptomyces.
the phosphate-dependent regulation of phosphate transport in S. coelicolor is more complex than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PhoP-regulated promoter of pitH1 and pitH2 is a novel example of the direct repeats of 12 bp recognized by the response regulator Phop.
PhoP is a global phosphate regulator in Streptomyces, which controls the expression of the phosphate transporters PitH2 and the phosphate-specific transport system PstSCAB.
PhoP, a member of two-component signal transduction systems, controls the expression of a high-affinity P(i)-transporter and a low-affinity transporter.
